items.title: Collegium recommends elevation of judicial officer Yash Paul Bourney as Jammu & Kashmir High Court judge
items.summary: The Supreme Court Collegium has recommended the appointment of judicial officer Yash Paul Bourney as a judge of the High Court of Jammu & Kashmir and Ladakh. The recommendation was approved by the Collegium at its meeting held on September 10 “ The Supreme Court Collegium in its meeting held on 10th September, 2026 has approved the proposal for appointment of Shri Yash Paul Bourney, Judicial Officer, as a Judge of the High Court of Jammu & Kashmir and Ladakh ,” the Collegium statement said. The statement is brief and does not disclose Bourney’s present posting or provide further details about the recommendation. The Collegium’s recommendation will now form part of the process for his proposed elevation to the High Court. Bourney is a District and Sessions Judge in the Super Time Scale and is currently serving on deputation as Member of the J&K Special Tribunal, Jammu. He has been posted there since November 14, 2025. Born on August 25, 1967, Bourney entered judicial service on December 1, 1997. He entered his present cadre on August 30, 2011. [Read Collegium Statement]

items.title: A Fundamental Right
items.summary: With its new law that makes education a fundamental right with effect from April 1, 2010, India joins a small group of countries with such a statutory provision. items.summary: A Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) leader has moved Punjab and Haryana High Court to seek contempt of court proceedings against Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) co-convener Saurav Das for imputing political motives to High Court's recent direction for release of pending dearness allowance/dearness relief (DA/DR) of Punjab government employees and pensioners. The judgment was delivered by a Bench of Chief Justice Ashwani Kumar Mishra and Justice Rohit Kapoor on August 03. Justice Mishra was then the Acting Chief Justice of the High Court. The petition filed by advocate Nitin Garg, who is the State General Secretary of Bharatiya Janata Yuva Morcha (BJYM) Punjab Unit, the youth wing of BJP, alleges that Das on August 20 criticised the judgment and claimed that the matter was clandestinely withdrawn from another "independent bench" in violation of the roster. The plea accuses of Das of making false claims about the Court's judgment. Chief Justice Ashwani Kumar Mishra and Justice Rohit Kapoor The petition has not yet been cleared for listing by the registry.
